h1: The 5 Best Small Safes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five small safes for documents, cash and valuables, compared on capacity, bolts, backup access and mounting options.
summary: The Bonsaii 0.6 cu ft safe is our top pick for its roomy interior and three ways in, including USB-C emergency power. The Honeywell bolt-down model is best for anti-removal security, the 0.30 cu ft upgraded safe adds an alarm, the Voncabay gives clear light feedback, and the Yuanshikj is the budget buy.
intro: The biggest mistake with a small safe is trusting the lock and ignoring the floor. A safe you can pick up and carry away protects nothing, so mounting hardware matters as much as bolts and keypads.
We reviewed the listed specs of eight small safes and ranked five on size, locking bolts, backup access and anchoring. This is an on paper comparison of listings, not a security certification.

products.name: Bonsaii Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Home Office, 0.6 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: The roomiest safe here, with a real backup plan if the keypad fails.
products.description:
The Bonsaii measures 13.78 by 9.84 by 9.84 inches for 0.6 cubic feet, with a removable shelf and two 18mm steel locking bolts. You can open it by code, key or USB-C emergency power.

It ranks first because the interior is more than double the 0.23 cu ft models, and the USB-C backup solves the dead-battery problem. The tradeoff is a higher $50 to $100 price.

It suits home offices storing documents and a laptop. It is not a fire safe, so keep irreplaceable papers elsewhere.
products.idealFor: Home offices storing documents and small electronics.
products.skipIf: You only need to store a few items.

products.name: Honeywell Safes & Door Locks - Bolt Down Small Safe Box with Digital Lock
products.verdict: Built to be bolted down, not just locked.
products.description:
The Honeywell lists bolt-down mounting hardware with pre-drilled holes, a solid steel cabinet and door, two solid steel live lock bolts, a scratch-resistant black powder coat and two emergency keys.

It ranks second because anchoring is the strongest anti-theft feature in this group, while the Bonsaii wins on capacity. The $50 to $100 price is the same tier.

It suits renters and homeowners who can drill into a floor or shelf. It does not list a backup power option.
products.idealFor: Anyone who can anchor a safe to a floor or shelf.
products.skipIf: You cannot drill into your mounting surface.

products.name: [UPGRADED] Small Safes for Home, 0.30 Cuft Mini Safe Box
products.verdict: A mid-size safe with a wrong-entry alarm and a key recovery path.
products.description:
This 0.3 cu ft safe measures 10.63 by 6.69 by 6.69 inches with 42mm door thickness, two 20mm bolts and a wrong-entry alarm with a silent mode. A serial-number service replaces lost backup keys.

It ranks third because the bolts are thicker than the Bonsaii's 18mm, and the alarm adds deterrence, but the cabinet is half the size.

It suits apartments where a loud alarm helps. It sits in the $25 to $50 tier.
products.idealFor: Apartments where an alarm adds deterrence.

products.name: Voncabay Money Safe Box for Home with Digital Keypad, 0.23 Cu. Ft., Black
products.verdict: Clear light cues and a lockout after three wrong entries.
products.description:
The Voncabay lists 0.23 cu ft, an automatic interior light, a low-battery warning light, a 5 minute lockout after three wrong entries and a fireproof document bag.

It ranks fourth because the lights and lockout help daily use, but it is smaller than the 0.3 cu ft safe above and the fireproof bag is a bag, not a certified safe.

It suits small valuables and travel documents. It sits in the $25 to $50 tier.
cons: Bag is not a certified safe

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: The cheapest safe here, with mounting holes included.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj lists 0.2 cu ft, dual steel locking bolts, a magnetic auto-lock door, pre-drilled mounting holes and bolts included. It sits under $25.

It ranks last because the interior is the smallest, though the magnetic auto-lock and mounting hardware are generous at the price.

It suits students and first-time buyers. Anchor it to a surface to get real security.
products.skipIf: You need to store bulky items.

whatMatters.detail: A safe that can be carried off is a locked box, not a safe. Mounting holes and bolts let you fix it to a floor or shelf. Check the listing for pre-drilled holes and included hardware.
Locking bolts fix the door to the body. Thicker bolts, such as 20mm instead of 18mm, resist prying better. Look for the diameter in the bullet points.
Keypads run on batteries, and dead batteries lock you out. A safe with a key or USB-C emergency power avoids that. Check how many access methods the listing names.
0.23 cu ft barely fits a passport and some cash. 0.6 cu ft fits a laptop. Check the interior dimensions, not just the exterior.
A fireproof bag is not a fire-rated safe. Look for an actual fire rating if protecting papers matters. These listings do not claim one.

rows: A few items on a budget

cards.label: Backup access
cards.text: Protects you from lockouts. The Bonsaii adds USB-C power and the Honeywell includes two emergency keys.

cards.label: Anchoring
cards.text: Protects against theft of the whole safe. The Honeywell and Yuanshikj include mounting hardware.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to anchoring first, since a carried-off safe fails regardless of its lock.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A small footprint, mounting holes and a keypad with a backup key.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Yuanshikj is the cheapest and includes mounting hardware, and the Voncabay adds light feedback.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You store a laptop or need heavy anchoring, where the Bonsaii or Honeywell are the better fit.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You store only a few items, where the Yuanshikj covers the basics.

faq.q: Do small safes protect against fire?
faq.a: None of these list a fire rating. The Voncabay includes a fireproof document bag, which is not the same as a rated safe.

faq.q: What is the common small safe mistake?
faq.a: Skipping the mounting step. A safe that is not anchored can simply be carried away.

faq.q: Is the Honeywell worth it over the Yuanshikj?
faq.a: If you want solid steel and two live bolts, yes. The Yuanshikj also includes mounting hardware at a lower price.

faq.q: How do I mount a small safe?
faq.a: Use the pre-drilled holes and supplied bolts to fix it to a stud, shelf or floor.
The Bonsaii accepts USB-C emergency power, and the Honeywell has emergency keys.

faq.q: Can two people use one safe?
faq.a: Some models support multiple access methods, but the code-only options share one code.

finalTake: The Bonsaii 0.6 cu ft is the best all-around small safe. Pick the Honeywell if you can bolt it down, the 0.30 cu ft model for an alarm, and the Yuanshikj on a tight budget.
